extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and attorneys handling USPTO reciprocal-discipline matters
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on a state-bar suspension, describing service requirements, findings, suspension terms, publication/notice obligations, suspended-practitioner duties, and reinstatement procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Action taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director of the USPTO may impose discipline identical to that imposed by a State Bar through the reciprocal-discipline provisions in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, relying on statutory authority in 35 U.S.C. § 32.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for imposing reciprocal discipline under § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline may be imposed when a practitioner has been disciplined by a state authority for misconduct that violates the ethical standards applicable to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order referenced the State Bar of Texas decision in Commission for Lawyer Discipline v. James O. Okorafor and asserted violation of USPTO ethical standards as the factual basis for imposing identical discipline under § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's opportunity to oppose under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is provided an opportunity to file, within forty days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order informed Respondent of the forty-day deadline and the specific regulatory grounds on which a respondent may oppose reciprocal discipline; failure to timely respond permits the Director to find no genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and notice procedures (mailing to last known address and service by publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice and Order must be mailed by certified mail to the respondent at the last address known to the OED Director; if unable to serve, service by publication pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.35(b) may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order documents mailing (certified mail receipt) to the last known address; after returned mail and inability to serve, the USPTO served respondent by publication in the Official Gazette (dates provided). The published notice informed respondent how to request copies and the time frame to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of respondent's failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a timely response to the Notice and Order, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The analysis states that due to Respondent's failure to file a response, the Director determined (1) no genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d) and (2) suspension from practice before the USPTO is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of sanction (suspension terms)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director ordered suspension of the respondent from the practice of patent, trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO for two years, effective the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly directs a two-year suspension and sets an effective date as of the Final Order; this mirrors the discipline imposed by the State Bar decision cited as the basis for reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notification obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is directed to publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette and to give notice of the final decision to appropriate USPTO employees, interested departments, agencies, courts of the United States, and appropriate state authorities where the practitioner is known to be a member of the bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes the full text of the Notice of Suspension for publication and instructs the OED Director to notify internal and external stakeholders and state authorities of the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting of disciplinary decisions (public reading)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted for public reading at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (URL provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states where disciplinary decisions are publicly accessible, providing a means for public inspection and transparency of practitioner discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of suspended practitioner under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: A suspended practitioner must comply with the duties set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58, and must submit proof of compliance with specified subsections when filing a petition for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs Respondent to comply with duties under § 11.58 and to submit proof of compliance with § 11.58(b)(3), (b)(5), and (b)(6) to the OED Director upon filing a petition for reinstatement under § 11.60. (Though the Order cites the subsection numbers, the text of those duties is in the cited regulation.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedure (petition under § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: A suspended practitioner seeking reinstatement must file a petition for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 and demonstrate compliance with the duties required of suspended practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order conditions the ability to seek reinstatement on filing the petition under § 11.60 and submitting the proofs of compliance required by § 11.58 as directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order must be mailed by first class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the respondent at the address provided to OED pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11, with a certificate of service included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document includes a Certificate of Service certifying mailing to the respondent's address provided under the registration rules; proper service according to § 11.11 is documented as part of the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible relief and additional directives
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may direct such other and further relief as the nature of the cause requires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to suspension, the Order includes a catch-all directing other necessary relief (e.g., publication, notices, compliance requirements), indicating that the Director can tailor ancillary remedies and notifications.
